commits.message:
Markdown draws a GFM pipe table as Rich's Table (rich-demos-k78j.5yo)

A header row, then a delimiter row naming as many columns, is a table, read
as markdown-it reads one: tried before every other block, able to end a
paragraph, its body running to a blank line or a line that opens a block.
Each cell keeps its inline Markdown and sits where its delimiter's colons
put it; the header is drawn in markdown.table.header and the borders in
markdown.table.border, the styles and Table settings Rich uses.

Pinned against Rich 14's own output. Column widths are Table's, which
divides a squeezed width differently from Rich on purpose (table.ts
header), so a wide table wraps its cells at other columns than Rich's.

A host can ask when what it draws next changes (rich-animation-xi28.6rs)

Every animated primitive stamps its cells with the moment what they show
next changes, on `Style.nextChange`, which rides up through every container
as the anchor does and writes no byte. `Segment.nextChange` reads the
soonest off a composed frame: a `Frames` answers the next frame's start,
`Effected` what its effect says — a stepped signal and `onBeat` their next
step (`Beat.end`), a transition `t` until it is done and never after, a
plain loop `t` itself — and still content never, as `Infinity`.

`Effect` is now an interface: the call, and an optional `nextChange(t)`;
`withNextChange` attaches one, `nextChangeOf` is the one reading of an
absent one. `Clock.at(time, tick)` is the one-shot a host waits on, and
`Live` arms it after each frame — at the frame's next change or the rate's
next frame, whichever is sooner — so it draws each frame of a sequence held
shorter than its interval instead of a sample of them.

The showcase's brand carries a flash that declares its own schedule, and
its tagline counts down to the gauge's next step.
sparkle's doc says which edge a width change leaves its fireflies still on (rich-unfiled-791c.c8g5)

sparkle keeps its fireflies on a lattice that a width change cannot move (rich-unfiled-791c.c8g5)

Review of PR #415 found sparkle re-deriving its firefly count and stride from
each frame's width, so an element gaining one column could add a firefly
mid-flash or slide every home on a narrow one (0.21 of a 0.95 swing, measured).
Fireflies now sit one per PER columns along lattice rows ROWS apart, laid from
the element's first column and top row; the frame's extent only bounds which
slots are worked out, and a cell asks only the fireflies whose light can reach
it. A tall element is lit on every row, as the doc now says.

extent is a loop rather than a reduce allocating a tuple per value.

shimmer and sparkle cross the element where its frame lists cells (rich-unfiled-791c.c8g5)

A loop's Field is now handed the frame's Drawn, as a transition's Visibility
already is, and shimmer and sparkle read the element's columns (and sparkle
its rows) off Drawn.cells each frame. EffectTarget.span, the caller-stated
second source for that fact, is gone, as are the span arguments of shimmer
and sparkle and DrawnSubject.span in effects-feel.

A padded, wrapped or confined element was crossed at columns 0..span; it is
now crossed where it shows. Fireflies keep homes a fixed stride from the
element's first column, so an element that gains a column gains a firefly at
most rather than reshuffling every home.

The key echo names only the modifiers held and reads whole at its widest (rich-demos-k78j.4jr) (#414)

The echo spelled shift=false ctrl=false meta=false on every key, which pushed the row past the 100-column card after 100 claimed spaces and a Backspace. It now names only held modifiers; the widest row is 79 cells plus the claimed count. The row test asserts it reached that state and checks backspace, meta-backspace and fully-modified pagedown.
